//: navigationFallback is what makes a single-page app survive a HARD RELOAD or a
shared link. Without it, opening /records/email_013 directly asks the static
host for a file that does not exist and returns 404 — the router never runs.
That breaks the exact thing the URL-based filter state was built for: sending a
colleague a link to what you are looking at.
There is NO route-level auth here. Reads are open by design so a judge can
browse; writes are gated by a passcode header checked at the API. Putting auth
in front of the static host would gate reading, which is the opposite of what
is wanted, and would not protect the API at all.
